content.title: A conversation that actually closes the loop.
content.summary: Benchback turns parts-core returns into voice-guided, auditable workflows. From a mechanic’s inspection to the supplier credit that finally arrives.
content.problem: A shop ships a used part back. The deposit is still outstanding. A voice interface helps only if the return, the evidence, and the eventual credit stay in agreement.
content.built: A voice agent with scoped tools, server-owned workflow state, integer-cent transactions, revision checks, and idempotent credit reconciliation. Human approval stays explicit.
content.evidence: A fictional $240 deposit runs from inspection through dispatch and two partial credits. Unit, integration, and browser tests cover the lifecycle.
content.boundary: Working hackathon product. No paid pilot, ERP integration, carrier purchase, or automatic supplier submission is claimed.

content.title: A plan breaks. The evidence stays.
content.summary: A robotic workbench for inspectable interventions, recovery, and dual-arm task execution.
content.problem: An obstacle or lost grasp changes a robotic task. The system needs to explain why the next action is permitted.
content.built: A MuJoCo execution service, dual SO101 arms, learned joint-target proposals, numerical correction, OpenVINO safety signals, and event exports.
content.evidence: Backend simulation evidence is distinguished from the illustrative browser animation.
content.boundary: Simulation MVP, not a physical robot deployment, end-to-end VLA policy, or safety certification.

content.title: Every decision has a paper trail.
content.summary: RecallRoom follows an ingredient lot through finished products and shipments, with source quotations behind every relationship.
content.problem: A recalled ingredient can travel through multiple batches. Missing, uncertain, and corrected evidence must not be collapsed into false certainty.
content.built: Nemotron extraction with schema and evidence validation, human-approved records, asynchronous processing, and deterministic graph traversal without double counting.
content.evidence: A fictional food-recall scenario, documented provider run, fixture variants, and graph checks against an independent fixed-point oracle.
content.boundary: Evaluated MVP, not a certified food-safety product. No independent extraction accuracy, ERP connector, or automated customer messaging is claimed.

content.title: Leave yourself a way back.
content.summary: Unpause is a home for unfinished creative projects. Remember where you stopped, pick a small next step, and begin again.
content.problem: When you finally have ten spare minutes, remembering where you stopped should not consume all ten.
content.built: A local-first web and native experience with durable project storage, restart-safe timers, checkpoint history, portable backups, and purchase/restore integration.
content.evidence: Web and native tests, plus documented emulator and test-store evidence. A public web app and Android preview are available.
content.boundary: Projects stay on the device; accounts do not sync them. App-store launch, production billing, and remaining physical-device gates are separate.

title: Lotlight
content: Evidence-backed medical recall review for small clinics. Browser AI, exact identifier checks, human source review and documented response.

title: Annex
content: Compile AI regulation into executable controls with source evidence and reproducible benchmarks.

title: Raksha
content: A real-time scam-call shield: a second listener using Moss retrieval and explicit evidence.

content.title: An offer is not a promise.
content.summary: KindHandoff repairs disrupted family support plans with explicit helper acceptance and versioned handoffs.
content.problem: One cancellation can break several dependent arrangements. Suggesting a replacement does not mean they agreed.
content.built: A Streamable HTTP MCP server, scoped tokens, separate helper sessions, dependency gates, and versioned acknowledgements.
content.evidence: A reproducible multi-session flow and inspectable MCP trace with fictional households.
content.boundary: Alexa+ browser simulation is labeled. Native Alexa+ deployment is a separate step.

title: Looplight
content: Review care evidence and follow-up with a local model and a shared workspace.

title: KindHandoff Guard
content: MIT-licensed TypeScript guard for explicit handoff acceptance, auditable state transitions, and explainable candidate ranking. Zero runtime dependencies.

title: Granted
content: The AI grants team for small nonprofits. Live funding discovery, eligibility checks, reviewed proposals, and a practical workspace.

title: Lotline
content: Lotline helps clinic operations teams review recalls, reconcile affected inventory, and preserve response evidence.

title: Epilogue
content: An agent for after-loss administration, with explicit decision gates and a durable task ledger.

title: Catchment
content: Make the next sample count: transparent citizen stream evidence, constrained field sampling, and One Health follow-up. By Shivam Gupta.

content.title: A phone call is not a closed rental.
content.summary: Separate billing cutoff, collection, and return evidence when closing equipment rentals.
content.problem: “We’ll collect it tomorrow” does not establish when billing stops.
content.built: CALL-E integration, persistent request identity, idempotency keys, account budgets, and transcript-grounded extraction.
content.evidence: Offline workflow and Firebase emulator checks; public rehearsal uses labeled synthetic transcripts.
content.boundary: A real owned-number CALL-E test has not been conducted. No verified supplier pilot or savings claim.

title: OfferLoop
content: A job-search CRM with grounded drafts, application tracking, follow-ups and analytics.

content.title: A little less predictable.
content.summary: A personality sitcom with original characters, private local answers, and a scoring system that shows its working.
content.problem: A playful quiz can still respect privacy and explain why it reached its result.
content.built: Thirty-six scenes, sixteen original characters, transparent TypeScript scoring, a Python reference implementation, and browser-generated sharing cards.
content.evidence: Scoring parity and browser tests cover the journey. Answers stay local to the browser.
content.boundary: Entertainment, not psychometrics or a personality diagnosis.

content.title: A globe full of human contradictions.
content.summary: Anonymous city-level experiences, a shared reveal, and a deliberate privacy boundary.
content.problem: Small samples can expose participants or create misleading results.
content.built: An interactive geographic globe, accessible list, retry-safe submissions, frozen reveals, deletion receipts, and metric suppression.
content.evidence: Illustrative fixtures remain separate from real submissions. Database rules enforce reveal boundaries.
content.boundary: Season 001 has ended. Preview data is fictional and not a representative research dataset.

content.title: Test the test before you trust the score.
content.summary: Broken, incomplete, and golden controls calibrate coding tasks across five languages.
content.problem: A benchmark may accept a shortcut or reject its own reference solution.
content.built: A Python control plane, manifest validation, fresh workspaces, overlay allowlists, distinct failure classes, and normalized report hashes.
content.evidence: Five language packs and fifteen committed control reports. The browser replays those reports.
content.boundary: An evidence viewer, not a browser runtime for arbitrary code. The local runner assumes trusted task authors.

content.title: Better agents start with trustworthy environments.
content.summary: Real repositories become verifiable training and evaluation environments. Inspect the task, the patch, and the reward.
content.problem: A coding-agent score is only useful when its tests really distinguish a working solution from a plausible shortcut.
content.built: Declarative repository tasks, a reset/step interface, composable graders, protected test files, sandbox adapters, and golden/no-op validation.
content.evidence: Executable examples and a Python test suite verify task lifecycle and grading. The site explains how to build and validate an environment.
content.boundary: A framework and example environments; not a claim that a frontier model was trained or improved. Local execution is not hostile-code isolation.

content.title: Keep the failure. Lose the noise.
content.summary: Reduce a long event trace into a smaller reproducible regression case without losing its dependencies.
content.problem: A long trace makes a bug difficult to explain. Removing events carelessly can remove the bug or change what failed.
content.built: A Python reduction engine with dependency closure, pinned events, failure signatures, oracle budgets, a deletion audit, and a fresh final replay.
content.evidence: The bundled cache fixture reduces 36 events to 6. Native/browser engine parity is tested.
content.boundary: This fixture is not a universal reduction rate. A minimal trace is not proof of root cause or a global minimum.

content.title: Rehearse the failure before it costs you.
content.summary: A retry-policy simulator and trace inspector for understanding what happens when a tool commits an action but loses the response.
content.problem: A payment can succeed while its acknowledgement disappears. A blind retry can charge twice.
content.built: A deterministic workflow simulator, local trace inspector, and zero-dependency Python SDK for recording and injecting tool failures.
content.evidence: A checkout regression compares duplicate charges with guarded recovery. The browser makes each decision and resulting effect inspectable.
content.boundary: A fixed-workflow simulator and testing toolkit. Outcomes describe scripted experiments, not general model performance.

content.title: The tool failed. Did the action?
content.summary: ToolStorm makes agent failures reproducible. Lose an acknowledgement, inspect the committed effect, and find out what a retry really does.
content.problem: A shipment succeeds but its response disappears. An unchecked retry creates a second shipment. Success and acknowledgement are different events.
content.built: A zero-dependency Python library for seeded tool failures, explicit side effects, call budgets, virtual clocks, and strict offline replay. The browser lab runs the same Python in Pyodide.
content.evidence: Native/browser parity and property tests cover fault and replay behavior. The public lab lets you compare recovery policies.
content.boundary: Scripted recovery experiments, not an LLM performance benchmark. Source-install beta; no PyPI release or production adoption claim.

title: SAT PDF to CSV
content: Extract text from SAT question PDFs and use a model-assisted parsing step to produce a reviewable CSV question bank.

title: AP FRQ Review
content: Review AP free-response questions in batches using configurable evaluation prompts, parallel requests and downloadable feedback.

title: AP Article Review
content: Review batches of AP learning articles against configurable quality prompts, inspect model feedback and export review results.

title: Math Question Editor
content: Edit, preview and export math question banks without manually restructuring each question. Supports JSON, tabular review and PowerPath-compatible output.

title: StepFree
content: An accessibility-repair workflow that combines coding agents with independent scans, content-integrity checks and human review.

title: Speechace Proxy
content: Keep pronunciation-scoring credentials server-side while forwarding bounded audio uploads to Speechace.

title: Background and approach to building products

content.source: First-person background and leadership strengths supplied by Shivam. These are his own account, not independently measured claims.

chapters.heading: Two ways of seeing. One way of building.
paragraphs: I studied Computer Science & Design at IIIT Delhi. It taught me to move between how a system works and how someone experiences it.
I bring both questions to a product: can we build it well, and will it make sense to the person using it? That is where my work starts.

chapters.heading: The work changes. Direction still matters.
paragraphs: I think of the next phase of work as an allocation economy: deciding where people, models and attention can do the most useful work.

One of my strengths is turning a product problem into work people can own. I delegate, manage people, and connect technical and non-technical teams. Clear briefs, shared context and thoughtful review help us ship together.

chapters.heading: Faster building. A more thoughtful brief.
paragraphs: As AI makes implementation faster, I see product management becoming more important: choosing what gets built, why it should exist, and who it helps. Fresh ideas start with noticing a real problem.

My background gives me three ways to work on that question. Human-centered design helps me understand people. Computer science helps me build the system. Product leadership helps a team choose and deliver the right work.

chapters.heading: Close to the customer. Through to delivery.
paragraphs: I value forward-deployed engineering because it keeps the customer conversation close to the build. I’ve worn that hat alongside technical product management: meeting customers, understanding requirements, and helping them deploy the product.

I enjoy the work between an idea and something people can use. For me, engineering, design and leading people belong in the same process: carrying fresh thinking into a product that works for someone.

title: Agent reliability lab
content: A deterministic local JavaScript simulation, not a live LLM test. Visitors select lost acknowledgement, service unavailable, or malformed response; choose stop, blind retry, or idempotent retry plus validation. A lost acknowledgement after a committed shipment causes blind retry to create two shipments. A stable operation key and response validation recovers one verified shipment. Runnable Python export reproduces each configuration. Inspired by ToolStorm and Agent Rehearsal; not the complete library.
